ownerDecisions.summary: Keep the official upstream binaries, pinned; a reviewed class for host-OS and statically linked system libraries with exact entries (glibc LGPL-2.1-or-later, libseccomp LGPL-2.1-only, libpathrs MPL-2.0 OR LGPL-3.0-or-later electing MPL-2.0, nft GPL-2.0-only as a separately executed host program); source offers from the pinned tags.

An OR-choice rule (an "A OR B" expression with an allowed alternative is accepted, electing it, recorded per component) and exact entries for GPL-3.0-or-later WITH GCC-exception-3.1 and the nft library closure in the host-OS class; gmp elects LGPL-3.0-or-later.

An AND-term rule (a compound is accepted when every AND term is allowed, an allowed exception, reviewed or OR-resolved) and legacy "A/B" crate strings read as "A OR B" with the normalisation recorded; the build-time license gate and SBOM produce the crate list and elections.

neverFor: code copied into a planeon repository
a container runtime or other component that owner decisions do not name

orChoice.rule: An expression "A OR B ..." is accepted when at least one alternative is accepted on its own for the component. The election ranks the accepted alternatives: Apache-2.0, then default-allowed, then an allowed exception, then open content (artifacts only), then the host-OS class, then an approved explicit-review license, ties broken by the canonical text; an owner-named election (ownerElections) applies to its named component whatever the term order. Each election is recorded per component as its canonical OR group and the elected alternative.

andTerms.rule: A compound "A AND B ..." is accepted when every AND term, after resolving parenthesised OR terms, is accepted on its own; the obligations are the union of the terms' obligations.

legacySlash.rule: A Cargo crate license field written "A/B" (legacy crates.io syntax) is read as "A OR B"; the normalisation is recorded in the SBOM. It applies to crate metadata only.

scope.rule: A host-OS class term is accepted only for a component of kind HOST_OS_PROGRAM, HOST_OS_LIBRARY or STATIC_SYSTEM_LIBRARY in UPSTREAM_PINNED custody; an explicit-review approval only for its named subjects; an open-content term only for an ARTIFACT. Elsewhere such a term is OUT_OF_SCOPE, which ranks with UNKNOWN. The scope applies inside AND and OR compounds too.

rules.precedence: Expressions are compared in canonical form (nested operators flattened, operands sorted, single spaces), and a compound listed exactly in the base policy keeps its base outcome however it is spelled. An AND compound with a blocking term takes the most restrictive blocking outcome under the base evaluation.precedence (DENIED, then UNKNOWN or OUT_OF_SCOPE, then PLANNED_UNRESOLVED, then OPTIONAL_EXPLICIT_REVIEW); an OR expression with no accepted alternative takes its least restrictive alternative's outcome. No rule weakens the base deniedRule.
